metadata.title: Agent Harness.
metadata.note: Standalone teaching explainer (~3min). Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'AI, Explained'. FRAMEWORK-FIRST (built to pass PROOF): the reusable definition is shown before any example (B01), then THE LOOP (B02), a worked run (B03), a falsifiability/edge case (B04: chatbot vs agent — where's the loop?), and a scaffolded viewer task (B07). ONE insight: an agent isn't a smarter model — it's a model wrapped in a LOOP (the harness) with tools, that acts, observes the result, and decides again until a stop condition. The harness is the part you actually build and control. Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro via Claude Remotion comps); body B01-B05 are house-style 4K PIL cards generated by make_cards.py.

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. Everyone's talking about AI agents. But an agent isn't a smarter model, it's the same model dropped into a loop that lets it use tools and act. That loop is the harness. By the end, you'll be able to tell a real agent from a chatbot with confidence.

props.command: What's an “agent harness” — and what actually makes an AI an agent instead of just a chatbot?
output: a model, put in a loop

beats.narration_text: Definition first. Take a model, the brain. Give it tools, and wrap it in a loop that lets it act, see what happened, and decide again. That wrapper is the harness. So an agent equals a model, plus tools, plus the loop that runs them. The model thinks; the harness is what actually does things in the world.

show.event: the model chip and the tools chip sit on the left
arrows feed into the harness box (accent), which outputs actions

card.title: Model, Wrapped.
card.subtitle: the definition, first
card.caption: an agent = a model + tools, wrapped in a loop that lets it act, see the result, and decide again
card.footer: THE MODEL THINKS · THE HARNESS ACTS · THE LOOP REPEATS

beats.narration_text: Here's the loop the harness runs. One: decide the next step. Two: act, call a tool. Three: observe the result, what actually came back. Then loop, decide again with that new information. It keeps turning until the goal is met, then it stops. Observe is the key step. Without it, the model is just guessing in the dark.

show.event: the three nodes light in order: decide, act, observe
the terracotta repeat arrow loops back to the start

card.title: The Loop.
card.subtitle: what the harness runs
card.repeat_label: repeat — until the goal is met, then stop
card.caption: observe is the key step — without seeing the result, the model is just guessing in the dark

beats.narration_text: Watch it turn on a real task: fix a failing test. The model reads the error, then acts, it runs the tests. It sees them fail, edits the file, runs them again. Green. Goal met, it stops. Every turn, it acted and then looked at the result before the next move. That looking is what makes it an agent.

show.event: the failing-test tile and the goal feed the loop
the answer prints the turns: run, fail, edit, run, pass, stop

card.title: Watch It Turn.
card.subtitle: one real task, start to finish
card.answer: run tests → sees red → edits the file → runs again → green ✓ → stops
card.caption: every turn it acts, then looks at the result before the next move — that looking is the agent
card.footer: ACT → OBSERVE → ACT AGAIN · UNTIL GREEN

beats.narration_text: Now the tell. A chatbot: you ask, it answers, done. One turn, no tools, it never sees a result. An agent: it acts, observes, and decides again, and again, until it's finished. So ask two questions of any so-called agent: where's the loop, and who owns the stop condition? No loop, no observation? It's a chatbot with a costume on.

show.event: left pipeline: ask → answer → done (one turn)
right pipeline: act → observe → decide again (accent, loops)

card.title: Real Agent, or Costume?
card.subtitle: where's the loop?
card.left_note: one turn · no tools · never sees a result
card.right_note: loops until the goal is met
card.caption: no loop, no observed result? it's a chatbot in a costume — not an agent
card.footer: ASK: WHERE'S THE LOOP — AND WHO OWNS THE STOP?

beats.narration_text: And here's why the harness matters: it's the part you actually build and control. Which tools it can reach. When it's allowed to stop. What happens when a tool errors. How much it remembers. The model gets the headlines, but the harness is where the real engineering, and the real safety, lives.

show.event: five control cards snap in, one per responsibility
caption lands: the harness is where the engineering lives

card.title: What The Harness Owns.
card.subtitle: the part you actually build
card.caption: the model gets the headlines — the harness is where the engineering and the safety live

beats.narration_text: So next time someone says agent, run the test. It's a model in a loop, with tools, that acts and observes until it's done. Ask where the loop is, and who owns the stop. That's the harness, and that's the part that's really yours.

artifactLines: Definition: a model wrapped in a loop with tools — it acts, observes the result, and decides again.
The loop: decide → act (call a tool) → observe → repeat, until a stop condition is met.
The tell vs a chatbot: a chatbot answers once and never sees a result; an agent acts and observes, in a loop.
The test: ask “where is the loop, and who owns the stop condition?” — that’s the harness, the part you build.

beats.narration_text: Your turn, and this is a real exercise. Take a task you do in steps, say, triaging your inbox. Write down the tools an agent would need, and the exact rule for when it should stop. That stop condition is the hardest part, and writing it is how you learn what a harness really does.

props.command: Take a task I do in steps — like triaging my inbox. List the tools an agent would need, and write the exact rule for when it should STOP.
output: the stop condition is the hard part
tools + stop = the skeleton of an agent
